misconception_description: Student believes that the body of an if-statement executes repeatedly as long as the condition holds.

solutions.generated_code:
program JumlahMinMaks
kamus
  n, i, x, minimum, maksimum : integer
algoritma
  input(n)
  i <- 1
  if i <= n then
    input(x)
    if i == 1 then
      minimum <- x
      maksimum <- x
    else
      if x < minimum then
        minimum <- x
      endif
      if x > maksimum then
        maksimum <- x
      endif
    endif
    i <- i + 1
  endif
  output(minimum + maksimum)
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: The student rewrote the solution to manually find max and min values by "iterating" through the array. They use an if-statement with the condition `if index < len(nums):` and increment the index inside, believing this will continue executing and check all elements in the array (like a while loop would). In reality, the if-statement body only executes once, so only the element at index 1 is checked. This produces incorrect results for arrays with more than 2 elements. From the student's perspective, they believe they're properly iterating through all array elements to find the maximum and minimum values.
